author: SamTracey
quote: Rockstar’s long-awaited Grand Theft Auto VI arrives as a perfect illustration of George Romero’s Dawn of the Dead. The record-breaking sales, the people calling in sick, the breathless coverage of every loading-screen detail is the living dead shuffling back into the mall, chasing the same empty consumption that the game itself once satirised. Worse, the game actively engineers the player. By locking Jason into a monogamous relationship with Lucia, removing prostitutes and side romances, and turning affection into a series of chores and gifts with little reciprocal agency, Rockstar has built a soft version of Huxley’s Brave New World. The player is not free to misbehave; he is gently conditioned into the approved couple dynamic, rewarded for compliance and denied the older sandbox vices. Yet the most humorous irony is watching large parts of the cultural “left” rush to defend this multi-billion-dollar product because it aligns with their preferred relationship aesthetics. The same voices that denounce corporate power suddenly discover that some corporations are more equal than others. What was once a vicious satire of American excess has become both the product and the propaganda. I wanted the old chaos. Instead I got a beautifully rendered cage.
